abstract: Manages vessel trenching operational logs, dynamic positioning assessments, and subsea burial trial verifications
system_message:
You are Marine operations superintendent (MOPS). The Marine operations superintendent (MOPS) manages vessel trenching operational logs, dynamic positioning assessments, clear deck space verifications, and subsea burial trial verifications for candidate marine engineering consortia.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Manages vessel trenching operational logs, dynamic positioning assessments, and subsea burial trial verifications（OPSREC）
information_points.content:
MOPS-OPSREC-R4Y：For Seaway Oceanic Infrastructure Consortium, the seabed trenching trial protocol for the heavy subsea trenching ROV system was completed, confirming full wet sea trials and jetting tool deployment cycles. Its pre-qualification performance dossier records an average seabed burial trenching speed of 110 m/h in the glacial till and dense sand seabed test trench at the target 1.5-metre cable burial depth.
MOPS-OPSREC-IEB：For Cambrian Subsea Installation Group, the seabed trenching trial protocol for the heavy subsea trenching ROV system was completed, confirming completion of wet sea trials and jetting tool deployment cycles. The pre-qualification performance dossier demonstrates an average seabed burial trenching speed of 155 m/h in the glacial till and dense sand seabed test trench while maintaining the target 1.5-metre cable burial depth.
MOPS-OPSREC-JL3：For Celtic Oceanic Marine Services, the seabed trenching trial protocol for the heavy subsea trenching ROV system was completed, confirming full execution of wet sea trials and jetting tool deployment cycles. The pre-qualification performance dossier shows an average seabed burial trenching speed of 155 m/h across the glacial till and dense sand seabed test trench while maintaining the target 1.5-metre cable burial depth.

information_points.title: Clear deck space verification（DECKAREA）
information_points.content:
MOPS-DECKAREA-A6L：According to the vessel general arrangement plan for Cambrian Subsea Installation Group, the primary cable-laying vessel deck provides 1,100 m2 of certified cargo deck area certified as unobstructed usable working deck space for cable carousel loading.
MOPS-DECKAREA-JQG：According to the vessel general arrangement plan for Celtic Oceanic Marine Services, the primary cable-laying vessel deck provides 1,600 m2 of certified cargo deck area, representing unobstructed usable working deck area certified for cable carousel loading.
MOPS-DECKAREA-KQB：According to the vessel general arrangement plan for Seaway Oceanic Infrastructure Consortium, the primary cable-laying vessel deck features 1,350 m2 of certified cargo deck area certified as unobstructed usable working deck space for cable carousel loading.
